topic.angle: From frog legs to the first battery

card.title: The pile that started the battery age

panels.text: 1780s, Italy. Luigi Galvani finds that a circuit of two metals and a frog's leg makes the leg respond.
In 1794 Alessandro Volta shows that you do not need the frog: two metals and brine-soaked cloth or cardboard in a circuit also produce an electric current.
In 1800 he stacks several pairs of copper (or silver) and zinc discs, separated by brine-soaked cloth, which increases the total electromotive force. Connect the top and bottom, and a current flows.
Today the idea lives on in every battery: its negative terminal is the source of electrons, which flow through your device to the positive terminal.

probes.question: In a battery that is supplying power, electrons flow out of which terminal?
True or false: Volta's 1800 pile stacked alternating metal discs separated by brine-soaked cloth.
